question: Can a fixed deterministic delimiter reset restore a nonconstant global first-unit entry-state channel excluded under unchanged-state continuity in GDT1319?

decision_note.genuinely_unknown: The GDT1319 contract excluded resets explicitly. Whether allowing the same arbitrary deterministic gap operation changes the active entry-state ceiling can be settled algebraically on its existing connected graph.
decision_note.outcomes: If counterexample exists, preserve reset as a live escape for informative entry states; if proof succeeds, close that particular repair without fitting a decoder. General stateful writers remain open either way.
decision_note.smallest_test: Relabel each old exit node O_g as J_g=R(O_g); verify connectedness on existing saved edges, prove consequence, supply noninjective countermodel to overclaim about exit states. No new source census or raw TSV.

contract.units_and_groups: Exactly GDT1319 strict complete groups, 22 working units, original-index-consecutive within-line pairs and separate readers; source and unit premises inherited.
contract.entry: For every active initial unit h, I_h is the complete entry state claimed by this particular explicit-marker channel. Values do not vary by occurrence, page or context.
contract.exit: For every active terminal unit g, O_g is a fixed exit state; word interior process and payload are otherwise unrestricted.
contract.delimiter: One deterministic total function R maps exit states to next entry states on every retained seam. R may be noninjective, constant, infinite-state, and unknown. There is no extra seam-varying command, context, position, randomness or hidden input.
contract.equation: I_h = R(O_g) on every retained edge (O_g,I_h).
contract.extension: R=identity recovers GDT1319. Arbitrary R is a genuine syntactic enlargement of that contract, but the proof is an elementary reparameterization rather than new manuscript evidence.

proof: Define J_g=R(O_g) separately for each active terminal unit.
Every old seam then asserts J_g=I_h; replace O-node labels by J-node labels without changing graph topology.
The saved GDT1319 graph is connected separately in each reading. Equality propagates through all its nodes, so one constant c satisfies every active I_h=c and every J_g=c.
Hence no fixed deterministic delimiter reset can restore two distinct active entry states in this channel. This holds for arbitrary state-set size and without R being injective.
If R is injective on the observed exit values, all active O_g also coincide, at some d with R(d)=c. Neither d=c nor unreachable-state constancy is implied.
For noninjective R, exits need not coincide: only their membership in the same preimage R^-1({c}) is forced.

sharp_countermodel.state_set: {0} union one distinct e_g for each active terminal glyph
sharp_countermodel.entry: I_h=0 for every active initial glyph
sharp_countermodel.verification: Every existing edge satisfies I_h=R(O_g)=0 while all terminal exit values may differ. Thus an all-exit-states-constant conclusion for arbitrary resets would be false.
sharp_countermodel.interpretation: This is only a mathematical compatibility example, not a proposed native writer or a decoded source.

further_safe_corollary: The entry-state ceiling also holds if a fixed deterministic reset R_g is selected solely by the final unit, because J_g=R_g(O_g) is still one fixed value per exit-marker node. Do not infer exit equality for different R_g even if each individual map is injective.

limits: Only active marker nodes and inherited strict panel are covered; inactive markers remain unconstrained.
A changing reset selected by position, page, source command, both endpoint markers, or hidden state is outside this contract.
First/last multi-unit markers, word-body entry coding, occurrence-dependent glyph values and uncertain boundaries remain outside.
No phonemes, word meanings, semantic spacing, native alphabet or general stateful cipher exclusion follows.
This is a minor logical strengthening for a well-defined repair, not an additional corpus observation, independent confirmation or decipherment advance.
